title: Prototype, Test & Validation
description: Review of prototype planning, first article inspection, fit and assembly trials, design verification planning, mechanical, environmental, ingress, thermal and battery testing, regulatory pre-compliance, pilot builds and test reporting.

items.text: Each prototype build has written questions it must answer
items.hint: Write the purpose per build (e.g. ergonomics, mechanism feel, drop survival) before ordering parts; builds without questions waste money.

items.text: Looks-like and works-like prototypes are distinguished and their limitations documented
items.hint: A looks-like model can't validate strength, and a works-like rig can't validate ergonomics; state what each can and can't show.

items.text: EVT, DVT and PVT entry and exit criteria are defined
items.hint: E.g. DVT requires production-intent design and tooled parts; PVT requires production tooling, process and line. Record which criteria were waived.

items.text: Process fidelity of prototype parts vs. production is recorded for each test
items.hint: A printed or machined part behaves differently from a molded one (strength, anisotropy, knit lines, residual stress). Note which results must be repeated on tooled parts.

items.text: Additive prototypes use process and orientation appropriate to the question being answered
items.hint: Build orientation drives strength in FDM, SLS and MJF parts; record orientation and material on the build sheet.

items.text: Prototype quantities cover test sample sizes plus spares for failures and rework
items.hint: Count samples per test from the verification plan and add margin; running out of samples mid-DVT stalls the schedule.

items.text: Prototype builds are tracked with part revision, material and supplier per unit
items.hint: Serialize units and keep a build record so test results can be tied to the exact design revision.

items.text: Build schedule aligns with test lab bookings and tooling milestones
items.hint: Lab slots for regulatory and environmental tests often book weeks ahead.

items.text: First article inspection report covers every dimension and note on the drawing
items.hint: Ballooned drawing with each characteristic measured and recorded against tolerance. Missing characteristics hide out-of-spec features.

items.text: Critical and key dimensions are measured on a CMM or equivalent calibrated method
items.hint: Hand calipers are not adequate for tight-tolerance or datum-referenced GD&T features. Confirm the datum setup matches the drawing.

items.text: Measurement datums and fixturing match the drawing datum scheme
items.hint: Measuring from the wrong datum gives false passes or failures; review the CMM program setup with the supplier.

items.text: Material certifications are received and match the drawing callout
items.hint: Check grade, temper, resin grade and color code on the cert. Substituted materials are a common source of failure.

items.text: Finish, plating and coating verification is recorded (thickness, adhesion, color)
items.hint: Coating thickness gauge, tape adhesion test and color comparison against the approved standard.

items.text: Out-of-spec features are dispositioned with a documented decision
items.hint: Use-as-is, rework or reject, with engineering rationale. Undocumented deviations become the de facto specification.

items.text: Cosmetic parts are inspected under the agreed lighting and viewing conditions
items.hint: Compare against approved boundary samples and the cosmetic specification.

items.text: Incoming inspection plan for production defines sampling and characteristics for each part
items.hint: Base sampling on part risk and supplier history; focus on critical dimensions.

items.text: Every part assembles to its mating parts without forcing, trimming or rework
items.hint: Record any part that needed modification during the build; each is a design or tolerance issue to close.

items.text: Assembly trial uses the documented assembly sequence and specified tools
items.hint: Builds by engineers who improvise hide problems operators will hit. Use the draft work instructions.

items.text: Fasteners reach specified torque without stripping, cracking bosses or thread jumping
items.hint: Torque-to-strip and drive torque checks on production-material bosses; check margin between drive and strip torque.

items.text: Gaps, flushness and alignment between visible parts are measured against targets
items.hint: Use feeler gauges or a gap/flush gauge at defined points; record on a map of the product.

items.text: Cables and flex circuits route without pinching, stretching or interference
items.hint: Inspect each unit opened after assembly and after test; look for witness marks on cables.

items.text: Moving parts operate through full travel with no binding across the tolerance range
items.hint: Test units built from parts near both tolerance extremes where possible, not only nominal parts.

items.text: Disassembly and reassembly for service is demonstrated without damage
items.hint: Disassemble at least one unit per the service procedure and rebuild it; check snaps and seals still function.

items.text: Assembly time is measured and compared against the cost model
items.hint: Time each operation during the build; large deviations mean the cost model or the design needs updating.

items.text: Every requirement has at least one verification test, analysis or inspection in the plan
items.hint: Cross-check the requirements matrix against the test plan; list any requirement verified by analysis only and why.

items.text: Sample sizes are justified statistically or by a referenced standard
items.hint: State the confidence and reliability basis or the standard that sets the sample size. "Three units" without rationale won't survive an audit.

items.text: Pass/fail criteria are written and approved before testing begins
items.hint: Criteria defined after seeing results are not verification. Include what functional checks are done after each test.

items.text: Test units are production-intent in design, material and process, or the deviation is documented
items.hint: Record each difference and justify why it doesn't affect the result.

items.text: Test sequence is defined where tests are performed on the same units
items.hint: E.g. thermal cycling before drop reflects aging. Sequential testing can reveal failures that single tests miss.

items.text: Test procedures specify fixtures, equipment, settings and measurement methods
items.hint: Someone else should be able to repeat the test from the procedure alone.

items.text: Test equipment is calibrated and calibration status is recorded
items.hint: Record equipment ID and calibration due date in each test report.

items.text: Design verification plan is traceable to the design FMEA and risk controls
items.hint: High-severity failure modes and risk controls each need a verification activity.

items.text: Drop testing is performed per the specified height, surface, orientations and count
items.hint: Inspect for cracks, displaced parts and loss of function after each drop; a high-speed camera helps diagnose failures.

items.text: Transit drop and vibration testing is performed in the shipping packaging
items.hint: Use the defined transport test profile with production packaging.

items.text: Vibration testing is run to the specified profile, with resonance search where needed
items.hint: Check for loosened fasteners, fretting, connector unseating and cracked brackets afterward.

items.text: Mechanical shock testing is run to the specified pulse and axes
items.hint: Inspect mounts, heavy components and latches after test.

items.text: Impact testing is performed on exposed surfaces, windows and displays
items.hint: Apply the specified impact energy at the weakest location identified by analysis or inspection.

items.text: Mechanisms are life-tested to the duty-cycle count with margin
items.hint: Run hinges, slides, latches and gears to rated cycles plus a margin; measure force, play and wear at intervals.

items.text: Button and switch actuation is cycle-tested with force and travel measured before and after
items.hint: Use a cycle tester at the specified actuation force; check for feel change, sticking and cosmetic wear.

items.text: Hinge cycle testing measures torque and play retention over life
items.hint: Record hinge torque at intervals; loss of friction torque is a common complaint.

items.text: Snap fits are cycle-tested for the number of assembly/disassembly cycles required
items.hint: Measure retention force after cycling; check for stress whitening and cracks.

items.text: Threaded insert torque-out and pull-out strength is tested on production-material parts
items.hint: Heat-set and molded-in inserts depend on the boss design and process; test on tooled parts.

items.text: Fastener joint preload or clamp retention is checked after thermal and vibration exposure
items.hint: Plastic creep and relaxation lose preload; check prevailing torque after environmental testing.

items.text: Cable and connector strain relief is pull-tested to the specified load
items.hint: Apply load in the worst direction and confirm no electrical or mechanical damage.

items.text: Static and user-load tests confirm no permanent deformation or failure at the specified load
items.hint: Apply loads per the requirements; measure deflection and set after load removal.

items.text: Safety-critical load paths are tested to the required safety factor
items.hint: Test to failure where feasible to know the actual margin, not just pass/fail.

items.text: Thermal cycling is performed over the specified range and number of cycles
items.hint: Check for cracking, warping, loosening, seal failure and adhesive bond failure after cycling.

items.text: High-temperature storage and operation tests show no deformation or creep beyond spec
items.hint: Check fit and gaps after high-temperature exposure; plastic parts under load may creep.

items.text: Low-temperature tests confirm mechanisms, snaps and seals still function
items.hint: Many plastics and elastomers become brittle or stiff at low temperature; repeat functional tests cold.

items.text: Humidity or damp heat exposure shows no corrosion, delamination or dimensional problems
items.hint: Nylons absorb moisture and change dimension; check fits after exposure.

items.text: UV exposure testing confirms acceptable color change and property retention
items.hint: Run accelerated weathering per the spec; measure color shift and impact strength.

items.text: Salt fog or corrosion testing confirms coating and fastener performance
items.hint: Inspect plated parts, fasteners and dissimilar-metal joints for corrosion after test.

items.text: Chemical resistance is tested with the specified cleaning agents and disinfectants
items.hint: Wipe or soak per the cleaning instructions for the required number of cycles, ideally on parts under stress; look for crazing and cracking.

items.text: Chemical exposure testing covers sweat, sunscreen, oils or other substances in the requirements
items.hint: Test with the substances listed in the requirements; stressed plastics can crack under exposure.

items.text: Ingress tests are performed to the target IP rating per IEC 60529
items.hint: Use an accredited lab or the defined in-house setup; inspect internally for water and dust after testing.

items.text: Ingress tests are repeated after environmental and mechanical stress
items.hint: Seals often pass when new and fail after thermal cycling, drop or vibration.

items.text: Ingress tests use units built from parts at tolerance extremes
items.hint: Seal compression varies with stack-up; test the worst case.

items.text: Ingress testing is repeated after service disassembly and reassembly
items.hint: Gaskets may take compression set; check resealing.

items.text: Production leak test method and limits are correlated with IP test results
items.hint: If an air-decay or pressure test will be used in production, correlate its threshold to actual ingress failures.

items.text: Pressure vents and membranes are verified for function and sealing
items.hint: Check venting performance and water ingress through vent assemblies.

items.text: Component temperatures are measured at worst-case ambient and power
items.hint: Use thermocouples on critical components and compare to limits and analysis predictions.

items.text: Touch temperatures of accessible surfaces are measured against the requirement
items.hint: Measure surfaces the user can touch during and after operation.

items.text: Thermal measurements are compared with simulation and the model is updated if needed
items.hint: Large deviation means the analysis model or assumptions were wrong; see Thermal & Structural Analysis.

items.text: Fans and active cooling are tested for blocked-vent and failure conditions
items.hint: Check temperatures with blocked inlets or a failed fan and verify safe behavior.

items.text: Thermal interface materials are inspected for contact and coverage after assembly
items.hint: Disassemble a unit and check the pad or paste imprint.

items.text: Battery abuse and safety test plan is agreed with the cell supplier and test lab
items.hint: Coordinate crush, impact, short circuit and overcharge testing responsibility; do not run abuse tests without suitable facilities.

items.text: Battery compartment is inspected for cell damage after drop and vibration testing
items.hint: Check for cell dents, swelling, displaced cells or tab damage.

items.text: Cell swelling allowance is verified with aged or swollen cells
items.hint: Measure cell thickness at end-of-life and confirm housing doesn't load the cell.

items.text: Transport test samples are scheduled for battery shipping certification
items.hint: Sample and lead time requirements must be in the plan.

items.text: Battery temperature during charging and operation stays within the cell supplier's limits
items.hint: Measure cell surface temperature during worst-case charge and operation.

items.text: Pre-compliance testing is done for the mechanical requirements of the safety standard
items.hint: Run enclosure strength, impact, stability and accessibility checks in-house before formal testing.

items.text: Certification test lab is booked and sample requirements are confirmed
items.hint: Labs specify sample quantity, configuration and documentation; book early.

items.text: Flammability rating of plastic parts is confirmed by material certificates or listings
items.hint: Check UL 94 rating at the actual wall thickness and color used.

items.text: Biocompatibility evaluation per ISO 10993 is planned with an accredited lab
items.hint: Use final materials, colorants and processing; test samples must be representative of production.

items.text: Samples for biocompatibility testing are production-representative, including cleaning and sterilization
items.hint: Process changes after testing can invalidate results.

items.text: Cleaning and disinfection validation is planned for reusable devices
items.hint: Validate cleaning instructions with the specified agents and cycle count.

items.text: Regulatory test results are tracked and nonconformities are fed back into design changes
items.hint: Keep a log of each finding and its resolution.

items.text: T1 tool samples are reviewed against drawings and a tool correction list is issued
items.hint: Review dimensions, cosmetics, sink, flash and warp; record every change request with owner.

items.text: T2 and later trials close every item on the tool correction list
items.hint: Track each correction to closure; unconfirmed fixes resurface at production.

items.text: Process window for molded parts is documented by the molder
items.hint: Record the established process parameters and confirm parts pass at the window limits.

items.text: Process capability is measured on critical dimensions
items.hint: Rule of thumb: Cpk targets per the customer or quality plan, often 1.33 or higher on critical dimensions.

items.text: Golden samples are approved and stored for each part
items.hint: Signed and labeled reference parts for dimensional and cosmetic comparison.

items.text: Tooling sign-off is completed with supplier and customer
items.hint: Formal tool acceptance after samples meet spec.

items.text: Pilot build yield and defects are recorded and root-caused
items.hint: Pareto of defects with corrective actions before ramp.

items.text: Assembly fixtures and production test equipment are validated
items.hint: Gauge R&R on fixtures and testers for critical measurements.

items.text: Design verification tests are repeated on PVT units where earlier tests used non-production parts
items.hint: Confirm production tooling and process do not change results.

items.text: Every test has a signed report with unit IDs, configuration, procedure revision and results
items.hint: Reports without unit and revision traceability can't be reused.

items.text: Every failure is logged with a root cause analysis
items.hint: Use 5 Whys, fishbone or failure analysis; "tested again and passed" is not root cause.

items.text: Corrective actions are implemented and verified by retest
items.hint: Link each corrective action to the retest that proves it.

items.text: Test deviations and anomalies are recorded in the report, not just failures
items.hint: Unexplained behavior is often an early warning.

items.text: Verification summary links every requirement to its test result and status
items.hint: Close the loop on the requirements matrix.

items.text: Test photos and failed samples are kept for reference
items.hint: Label and store failed parts for later analysis.
